title: 'They want us out of Palestine': On the ground in the West Bank
gist: A ground report from the Bedouin village of Umm al-Khair in the South Hebron Hills documents accelerating, state-backed Israeli settlement expansion in the West Bank -- 34 new settlements in six months, 47 villages depopulated since January 2023 -- ahead of Israel's 27th October election, with finance minister Bezalel Smotrich's explicit 'mega-strategic' annexation plan and a UK policy shift (sanctions, a 'comprehensive reset') forming the key near-term catalysts.

themes.theme: Pace and mechanics of West Bank settlement expansion

insights.claim: The Israeli government has promoted and financed 34 new West Bank settlements in the six months before September 2026, and since January 2023 (when the current government took office) 47 Palestinian villages have been wholly depopulated, per UN figures.
insights.speaker: Donald Macintyre
insights.so_what: A quantifiable, accelerating pace of de facto annexation ahead of an election is a leading indicator for escalating international sanctions risk (UK, EU) against companies and financial flows tied to settlements.
insights.locator: paragraph on Netanyahu government changing the West Bank

insights.claim: In 2026 alone, 3,800 Palestinians were displaced due to settler violence, demolitions and evictions, and 23 Palestinians have been killed this year in settler attacks according to the UN, while settlers are explicitly timing land seizures ('creating new facts on the ground') ahead of Israel's 27th October election.
insights.speaker: Donald Macintyre
insights.so_what: Settler activity clustering around the election date suggests expansion is being used as a political lever, meaning the election outcome is a binary catalyst for whether the pace of annexation accelerates or faces domestic pushback.

insights.claim: Only 2 per cent of Palestinian building-permit applications in Area C (60 per cent of the West Bank, under full Israeli security and civilian control) are approved, while settler construction such as the Umm al-Khair caravans proceeds without permits and even a court-ordered construction freeze was reversed after the settlers simply accelerated building and moved families in overnight.
insights.speaker: Donald Macintyre
insights.so_what: Demonstrates that formal Israeli legal/administrative processes are structurally asymmetric and functionally unable to constrain settlement growth, meaning court rulings and permit regimes are not reliable predictors of on-the-ground outcomes for anyone assessing West Bank political risk.
insights.locator: paragraph on 98 per cent permit rejection rate

insights.claim: Since 7th October 2023, roughly 5,500 settlers have been drafted into regional defence battalions and now serve with military jurisdiction in the areas they used to attack as civilians, per the Israeli Center for Public Affairs (OFEK).
insights.speaker: Donald Macintyre
insights.so_what: Militarization of settler activity blurs the line between vigilante violence and state action, raising the bar for any future accountability mechanisms (sanctions, ICC/ICJ actions) to distinguish 'settler violence' from 'military conduct.'

insights.claim: Netanyahu cancelled entry permits for roughly 115,000 Palestinian workers who used to cross daily into Israel after 7th October 2023, and by end-2025 the UN reported 14 Palestinians shot dead attempting to cross illegally; this economic exclusion compounds pressure on West Bank communities alongside land seizure.
insights.speaker: Donald Macintyre
insights.so_what: Loss of ~115,000 cross-border jobs is a measurable economic-pressure lever being used alongside land seizure, useful for modeling humanitarian/economic deterioration timelines in the West Bank.

insights.claim: Finance minister Bezalel Smotrich, who is now in charge of civilian affairs in the West Bank, has openly described the settlement process as 'mega-strategic' and stated in February that in a 'next term' he intends to 'cancel the cursed Oslo Accords' and pursue 'sovereignty while encouraging [Palestinian] migration both from Gaza and from Judea and Samaria.'
insights.speaker: Donald Macintyre
insights.so_what: A sitting finance minister with direct authority over West Bank civilian affairs has stated an explicit policy goal of ending the two-state framework and encouraging population transfer -- this is a concrete, quotable policy commitment for anyone assessing the durability of the two-state solution as a base case.
insights.quote: finally…. cancel the cursed Oslo Accords and get on the path of sovereignty while encouraging [Palestinian] migration both from Gaza and from Judea and Samaria [West Bank]. There is no other long-term solution.
insights.locator: paragraph quoting Smotrich on Oslo Accords

insights.claim: In an unprecedented move, the head of IDF Central Command authorised seizure of Area A land (nominally under Palestinian Authority civil control and legally off-limits to Israeli settlement) to build a road connecting new settlements south of Jenin, and a local Fatah activist's 2023 prediction that Israeli settlers would be inside Nablus within five years now looks 'far more plausible' to the author.
insights.speaker: Donald Macintyre
insights.so_what: Encroachment into Area A -- previously considered the reddest of red lines under Oslo -- signals the annexation process is no longer confined to Area C, expanding the geographic scope of related sanctions/divestment risk.
insights.locator: paragraph on IDF Central Command and Nablus prediction

insights.claim: A June 2026 leaked letter from former Israeli establishment and security figures, including ex-PMs Ehud Barak and Ehud Olmert, accused the Netanyahu government of pursuing 'an ideology of ethnic cleansing' and allowing settlers to commit 'Jewish terrorism,' often with the assent or cooperation of the Israeli military -- a warning the author says has 'fallen on deaf ears' inside Israel.
insights.speaker: Donald Macintyre
insights.so_what: Criticism from Israel's own former security establishment, not just outside human-rights groups, raises the credibility and political weight of ethnic-cleansing allegations, a factor relevant to ICJ/ICC-linked legal and sanctions risk.
insights.locator: paragraph on the June leaked letter

insights.claim: Israeli human-rights lawyer and activist Amiel Vardi argues that since 7th October 2023 there is 'complete collaboration of the authorities with the settlers' ideology and programme,' and that increasingly 'more and more soldiers in all ranks are either settlers or share the settlers' ideology.'
insights.speaker: Donald Macintyre
insights.so_what: A framework asserting ideological capture of the military itself (not just political leadership) implies institutional continuity of the annexation policy regardless of the October election outcome.
insights.quote: nobody tries to hide the complete collaboration of the authorities with the settlers' ideology and programme.

insights.claim: Settler Yinon Levi -- sanctioned by the UK, EU and US (until Trump reversed the US sanction) -- shot and killed Palestinian teacher and activist Awdah Hathaleen in July 2025 and was indicted in August 2026 for reckless manslaughter (max 12-year sentence), the first settler indicted for killing a Palestinian since 2019; he was released to house arrest after three days while villagers were held longer.
insights.speaker: Donald Macintyre
insights.so_what: A rare indictment, but a lenient charge and swift release, illustrates the practical ceiling on legal accountability for settler violence -- a useful data point for assessing whether Israeli judicial mechanisms will meaningfully constrain settlement-linked violence going forward.

insights.claim: The July 2024 International Court of Justice ruling that West Bank settlements are illegal, and that member states have a duty not to assist the occupation, has not altered facts on the ground; Netanyahu responded by declaring 'the Jewish people are not occupiers in their own land,' rejecting the ruling's premise entirely.
insights.speaker: Donald Macintyre
insights.so_what: Confirms that international legal rulings alone are not a binding constraint on settlement expansion; enforcement depends on state-level actions like sanctions (UK, EU) rather than the ICJ ruling itself.
insights.quote: the Jewish people are not occupiers in their own land—not in our eternal capital Jerusalem, nor in our ancestral heritage of Judea and Samaria.
insights.locator: paragraph on ICJ ruling and Netanyahu response

insights.claim: UK foreign secretary Ed Miliband announced on 1st September 2026 a planned 'comprehensive reset' of policy on the occupied territories, with sanctions curbing trade and economic activity with West Bank settlements expected in early September 2026.
insights.speaker: Donald Macintyre
insights.so_what: A concrete, near-dated UK policy catalyst (settlement trade sanctions) to monitor for direct impact on companies and financial institutions with West Bank settlement exposure.

themes.theme: Economic dismantling of Palestinian herding livelihoods

insights.claim: One Umm al-Khair resident's family flock has shrunk from roughly 500 free-grazing goats and sheep in the 1970s to about 20 pen-confined animals today, costing over $8,000 per season in store-bought feed -- more than he earns from milk and lambs -- because settler expansion has eliminated grazing land.
insights.speaker: Donald Macintyre
insights.so_what: Quantifies the mechanism by which land seizure converts a subsistence herding economy into a net-loss operation, forcing depopulation through economic attrition rather than direct violence alone -- a template applicable to other Masafer Yatta villages.

insights.claim: The neighbouring settlement of Carmel has 24/7 electricity (with power lines running over the Palestinian village to supply its industrial-scale chicken coops) while Umm al-Khair relies on unreliable solar power, and residents have only seven hours of access to the water grid per week.
insights.speaker: Donald Macintyre
insights.so_what: Illustrates a durable, quantifiable infrastructure asymmetry (utilities routed over but not to the Palestinian village) that functions as a structural incentive for depopulation independent of violence.
insights.locator: paragraph on electricity and water access

insights.claim: A Carmel settlement resident told France 24 that the outpost caravans surrounding Umm al-Khair are meant to 'remind them that we are here, watching everything' and will 'push them away from the settlement' so that 'little by little we will reclaim the land' -- an explicit statement of psychological-pressure strategy.
insights.speaker: Donald Macintyre
insights.so_what: A named, on-record admission of intent to displace via psychological pressure (rather than only legal/administrative means) strengthens the evidentiary basis for any future sanctions or legal action targeting settlement financing.
insights.quote: The [outpost] caravans are meant to remind them that we are here, watching everything that happens in the village. It will push them away from the settlement and little by little we will reclaim the land.
insights.locator: paragraph quoting Carmel resident to France 24

insights.claim: A British LSE student acting as a 'protective presence' activist was detained by settlers, accused (implausibly, per video evidence) of assaulting a child, held until police arrived, and deported two days later without charge -- illustrating that detaining and expelling foreign activists, even without legal grounds, is an effective settler tactic.
insights.speaker: Donald Macintyre
insights.so_what: Shows that international activist/observer presence, often relied upon by NGOs and diplomats as a check on settler violence, can be neutralized quickly via deportation -- reducing the reliability of that channel as an accountability mechanism.

insights.claim: In August 2026 Israel reclassified most of the section of Umm al-Khair previously recognised as privately owned by Palestinians as 'survey' land, which residents and observers see as a halfway step toward declaring it state land and allocating it to settlers.
insights.speaker: Donald Macintyre
insights.so_what: Identifies the specific bureaucratic/legal mechanism (private -> survey -> state land) used to formalize land transfer, a repeatable template for tracking future annexation moves elsewhere in Area C.
